title: tau2-telecom DtD v5f on the holdout with Claude Opus 5.5 as the customer, 3 trials per task (registered)
motivation: Reviewers asked for (i) the third controller on the held-out-fault pool, (ii) a stronger simulated customer for every arm, and (iii) repeated trials with pass^k, tau2's standard metric. All three in one registered run.
controller: the frozen v5f files in bounded_v5f_frozen (hashes in v5f_frozen_sha256.txt, registered in telecom-v5f, commit 51db041); unchanged
tasks: 60 tasks drawn from the 441 holdout tasks never used by an earlier evaluation (every holdout task contains break_app_storage_permission, a fault type absent from all fitting data; v5f's app-permission template names the storage permission, so this tests transfer of the fitted fault probabilities, not template coverage). Draw rule below; pulse at least 60 s after this file is hashed.
customer: Claude Opus 5.5 through the claude -p shim (system prompt replaced by tau2's user-simulator prompt; tools disabled; default reasoning; no temperature control, so trials differ)
arms: Qwen + v5f, fixed order, thinking fallback (temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95)
primary: success averaged over the 3 trials (pass^1), Qwen + v5f (thinking off) vs Qwen free, paired by task, task-clustered bootstrap (4000 resamples, seed 11); confirmed if the 95% interval excludes 0
targets_stated_in_advance: H1: Qwen + v5f (thinking off) pass^1 within 5 points of Opus alone (point estimate)
H2: Qwen + v5f with the thinking fallback pass^1 within 3 points of Opus alone (point estimate)
H3: Qwen + v5f pass^3 exceeds Qwen free pass^3 by at least 25 points
H4: LLM calls per conversation: Qwen + v5f < 2.5; Opus + v5f < 1.0

forecasts.Qwen free pass^1: 55-70% (the Opus customer lifted Qwen alone to 70% on draw-2 tasks)
forecasts.pass^3: about 5-15 points below pass^1 for the free arms, 0-6 below for v5f arms

metrics: pass^1 = mean success over trials; pass^k = share of tasks solved in all k of 3 trials (k = 1..3, tau2's definition); calls and agent tokens per conversation; customer messages per conversation; zero-call conversations.
reruns: episodes ending in an infrastructure error with no outcome are rerun once with the same code; counts reported per arm
reporting: every arm is reported whatever the result, in the paper's registration appendix
